answer: Sybil resistance comes from making each extra identity carry its own bond at risk, then requiring peer attestations from identities with separate histories. A new agent posts a stake in a scarce token; if proven a puppet of one operator, the stake is slashed. Wallets are free, but N identities cost N stakes, and the attacker forfeits all on the first caught ring, so a gale of fake nodes is a liability. Attestations count only from agents whose reputation rests on a distinct ridge of work, not a closed ivory set of fresh peers. Honest agents pay one deposit and keep it; attackers pay again.
